=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:
  SPA-N-001: General liability cap
  SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Positions

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package is not acceptable as drafted. Most of its protections for the Seller would also remove the Buyer's remedies for the issues already identified in due diligence. The "FINAL / not to be re-opened" label does not bind the Buyer until the SPA is signed.

**Priority order:** N-006/007 (disclosure and knowledge), N-008/009/011/012 (identified exposures), N-001/004/014 (cap and category structure), N-015 (title), then the remaining items.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** A higher general cap, ideally 100% of price for general warranties, with fundamental and tax claims outside it. Known exposures (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay) should be handled by specific indemnities, so they do not use up the general cap.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and counter higher.
- **Reason:** A AUD 4.8m cap is below the combined value of several identified exposures, which would leave the Buyer largely uncovered.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket (about 1% of price), with only the excess recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis around AUD 10,000 with related claims aggregated; a "tipping" basket that recovers from the first dollar once threshold is crossed, set at roughly 0.5% of price.
- **Recommendation:** Counter.
- **Reason:** As a deductible, the first AUD 250,000 of loss is unrecoverable, so the Buyer bears the first loss in full.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months from Completion for general claims, applied to all Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** 24–36 months for general warranties, so the Buyer covers at least one full post-Completion audit and tax cycle. Longer periods for fundamental and tax claims (see N-004 and N-016).
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24–36 months for general claims.
- **Reason:** 18 months may expire before the first full year-end and tax cycle after Completion is audited.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority) capped at price, outside the general cap and basket, with a limitation period of at least six years, subject to confirmation of the NSW position with local counsel.
- **Recommendation:** Reject.
- **Reason:** Title to the shares is what the Buyer is paying for, so it cannot sit under a general regime.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Not addressed. The exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses (9.3, 12.8, 20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out so that the cap, de minimis, basket, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions do not limit claims for fraud, including fraud by the Seller or Company personnel.
- **Recommendation:** Insert.
- **Reason:** As drafted, the "all Claims of any nature" wording would capture fraud claims; the Buyer should not rely on general law to protect them.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (to 5.00pm 22 September 2026), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete general disclosure. Disclosure only against specific warranties, fairly disclosed, with no deemed disclosure of data room or public-register contents.
- **Recommendation:** Reject.
- **Reason:** General disclosure of the whole data room would disclose every known issue at once and remove warranty protection for them.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete. Insert a pro-sandbagging clause confirming that the Buyer's rights are unaffected by its knowledge, and rely on specific indemnities for known issues regardless of knowledge.
- **Recommendation:** Reject.
- **Reason:** The Buyer already knows of the identified issues, so this clause would bar warranty claims on exactly the matters that matter most.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The conditions in clause 11.3 are not addressed.
- **Buyer wants:** Bluefen consent as a condition precedent to Completion, in final form, with evidence that all clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied. No deemed satisfaction. A walk-away right or price adjustment if consent is not obtained, plus a specific indemnity for revenue loss.
- **Recommendation:** Make it a condition precedent and reject deemed satisfaction.
- **Reason:** Bluefen represents about AUD 3.6m (roughly 30%) of FY26 revenue, and consent alone may not satisfy the clause 11.3 conditions.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to be provided after Completion. No final discharge of security yet.
- **Buyer wants:** Repayment at Completion through the funds flow, with a payout letter and PPSR discharge of security delivered at Completion. Repayment should be deducted from price on the debt-free basis.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release.
- **Reason:** Under a debt-free basis the debt must be settled out of price at Completion, and a post-Completion release leaves security over the Company's assets with the Buyer as owner.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 of conditional Completion bonuses, not in the funds flow. Payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs not addressed.
- **Buyer wants:** Treat the bonuses, plus associated payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs, as debt-like items deducted from price, or borne by the Seller. Update the funds flow.
- **Recommendation:** Treat as debt-like.
- **Reason:** Transaction-triggered bonuses are a Seller cost on a cash-free, debt-free deal, and they are currently missing from the funds flow.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; the Seller considers this adequate.
- **Buyer wants:** A specific indemnity covering all Ironquay claims and any unpaid fees. Payment of the AUD 180,000 open amount before or at Completion (or a retention), and a confirmatory IP assignment of SOW3 materials as a condition precedent.
- **Recommendation:** Reject.
- **Reason:** Title to the SOW3 materials depends on payment (DD-004 cl 7.3), and the Seller has not evidenced that the AUD 180,000 has been paid.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material.
- **Buyer wants:** Forensic investigation before signing. A specific indemnity for all incident losses, including regulatory, notification and remediation costs, with a separate cap and an escrow or retention. A warranty that there have been no other incidents. Buyer consultation rights over notifications.
- **Recommendation:** Specific indemnity plus escrow.
- **Reason:** About 1,240 records of personal information (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) were sent to an unintended external address, and whether they were accessed is unknown. Whether notification is required under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) also needs assessment, so the Seller's "not material" characterisation is unsupported.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 (3 × AUD 110,000) are ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** Confirm terms, duration, termination rights and whether any renewal extends beyond Completion. Treat accrued or pre-Completion amounts as debt-like. Warranty that there are no other undisclosed supplier commitments.
- **Recommendation:** Clarify and treat accrued amounts as debt-like.
- **Reason:** The DD-008 and DD-011 records do not say whether the renewals are unavoidable or multi-year, so the ordinary-course label cannot be accepted without evidence.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** One regime (cap, time limit, knowledge qualifier, disclosure) for all claims.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate categories with separate protections: general warranties (higher cap, 24–36 months); fundamental warranties (price cap, long limitation); tax (price cap, ATO limitation period plus 60 days); IP; and specific indemnities (separate caps, not subject to the general regime).
- **Recommendation:** Reject the single regime.
- **Reason:** A single regime lets the general cap and 18-month limit erode protection on title and tax.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the share register at DD-012 (Harbourglass Ventures holds 100%).
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification before signing: current ASIC company extract, the full share transfer history, a certified copy of the register, a PPSR search over the shares, confirmation of no options or convertibles, and delivery of share certificates and transfer forms at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Verify independently before signing.
- **Reason:** The Seller's register is the source being verified, not verification in itself, and DD-012 expressly does not confirm the Buyer's own checks.

### SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties settled under the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** A specific pre-Completion tax indemnity (covering income tax, GST, PAYG, payroll tax and superannuation), with a longer limitation period. IP warranties covering ownership of key IP (including the Ironquay materials and source code) under fundamental-level protection.
- **Recommendation:** Reject.
- **Reason:** Tax and IP liabilities often surface after 18 months, and the general regime would not protect against them.

---

**Caveats:**
- The Seller's "market context" (10–20% caps, 1% baskets, 12–18 month limits) is their assertion. Verify it against recent SaaS precedent before using it in negotiations.
- This is a first-pass commercial review, not legal advice. Points on NSW limitation periods, fraud carve-outs, sandbagging and Privacy Act obligations should be confirmed by NSW and privacy counsel.
- Figures are taken from the Seller's summary and disclosure letter. Confirm them against the underlying data room documents (DD-002 to DD-012).
